title: Billing Alarms & Budgets 💸
description: Never get a surprise bill: set up budget alerts and billing alarms.

slides.title: Why Billing Alarms? 🚨
slides.content:
# Fear the Surprise Bill

Stories of accidental $10,000 AWS bills are real – usually from forgetting to delete resources. Billing alarms don’t cap spending, but they **warn you** before it spirals.

- **Billing alarm**: A CloudWatch alarm that triggers when estimated charges exceed a threshold.
- **Budget**: A set limit with optional email alerts at certain thresholds (e.g., 80% of budget).

Set both as soon as you sign up.

slides.title: Creating a Billing Alarm 📊
slides.content:
# Step-by-Step

1. Go to **Billing and Cost Management** → **Budgets**.
2. Click **Create a budget**.
3. Choose **Zero spend budget** (free) or set a monthly amount like $10.
4. Add an alert threshold (e.g., 80% of budgeted amount) and enter your email.

AWS will email you when forecasted costs exceed the threshold.

> Note: Billing data is updated once daily. Alerts may lag by up to 24 hours.

quizData.question: What does a billing alarm do?

options.text: Automatically stops all your running resources to avoid charges
Notifies you via email when estimated charges exceed your threshold
Prevents you from launching expensive resources
Caps your spending at the set amount

quizData.explanation: AWS billing alarms are alerts, not caps. They rely on CloudWatch metrics and SNS to send notifications. You still need to manually stop resources.

slides.title: CloudWatch vs Budgets 🆚
slides.content:
# Which One to Use?

- **Budgets** are simpler, set in the Billing Dashboard, can track costs/reservations, and send email alerts.
- **Billing alarms** are CloudWatch alarms that use the `EstimatedCharges` metric and can trigger more complex actions (e.g., send to Slack, trigger Lambda).

**Recommendation**: Start with a zero‑spend budget (free) and add a CloudWatch billing alarm for $5.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Check the Cost Explorer 🔍
slides.content:
## See Your Spending Trends

The **AWS Cost Explorer** lets you visualise your costs and drill down by service. Even if you’re in Free Tier, it’s good practice to check monthly.

It can show you which services are costing you the most – and warn you about forgotten resources.
